I am not a legal expert, but I can provide some general tips on how to structure your will to minimize inheritance taxes:

1. Use a revocable trust: a revocable trust is a legal arrangement where you transfer your assets to a trustee, who manages them for your benefit. You can then revoke the trust at any time, and the assets will be distributed to your beneficiaries according to your wishes. This can help reduce estate taxes and avoid probate, which can be costly and time-consuming.

2. Donate assets to charity: if you have assets that you don't need, consider donating them to a charity. This can help reduce your taxable estate and provide a tax deduction for your donor.

3. Use life insurance: life insurance policies can be a valuable way to transfer wealth to your heirs. You can name beneficiaries on the policy and use the proceeds to pay estate taxes.

4. Avoid using beneficiary designations: beneficiary designations on retirement accounts and life insurance policies can create conflicts and disputes among heirs. Instead, use a revocable trust or other legal arrangement to transfer your assets.

5. Consult with a lawyer: a lawyer can help you structure your will and other legal arrangements to minimize inheritance taxes. They can also help you understand the tax implications of different strategies and advise you on the best course of action for your specific situation.
